how: Each version's percent = (done weight + half of partial weight) / total weight, where an item's weight is its effort size (default 1; big items such as calibration, hosting or the sandbox count 2 or 3). 'Core' = V0 to V4 and 'full' = all versions, both weighted by version size. Statuses are my honest reading of docs/STATUS.md; edit this file when reality changes.

limits: Nobody except the author has used it. Quality was judged by me, automated checks and AI judges.
Scores and ranking weights are first guesses, not calibrated against real opinions.
The human review of the first 10 reports was waived, so they are machine-verified only.
Only AI/ML-style goals have been tried. Languages beyond Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and notebooks get partial analysis.
An audit can be wrong too, and its judge sees the same evidence as the writer. Cited does not mean complete.
Free-tier model providers change and rate-limit without warning; narration can fail and is retried, never invented.

Accounts and hosting have only been tested on one machine with a handful of fake users. The Dockerfile has never been built, the first real deployment will find problems, and cloning arbitrary repositories on a shared server needs disk and time limits that are not set yet.
